paragraphs.english: Nora visited a flower shop just before closing time to buy a present for her mother. She had enough money for a small bunch of flowers, but she could not decide which color to choose. The owner asked where her mother usually spent the evening. Nora said she often read beside a window in a room with pale yellow walls. The owner placed two bunches against a yellow sheet of paper so Nora could compare them. Nora chose purple flowers. As the owner wrapped them, a boy came in carrying an empty bucket. Without asking, he began putting the outdoor signs inside and sweeping near the door. The owner thanked him and asked whether his homework was finished. He nodded and continued working. Nora noticed a family photograph beside the cash register that showed the owner with the same boy. When she left, the shop lights were still on, but the signs were gone and the door was ready to close.

paragraphs.english: A sports festival asked students to help with several jobs. A board in the hall had a column for each job, and students wrote their names under the one they preferred. The music column filled quickly. So did the column for handing out prizes. By Thursday, only the column for collecting equipment after the festival was almost empty. Hana had hoped to help with music, but she saw that twenty students had already chosen it. She wrote her name under equipment and asked two friends to join her. On festival day, the teachers had to make fewer calls for help than in previous years. When everyone else began leaving, Hana's group carried boxes back to the storage room. The music team finished early and came to help them. Hana was tired, but she smiled when she saw that no teacher had to stay alone in the dark playground. The next year, the board included suggested numbers of helpers for each job.

Mr. Park sat beside Emi and opened the box slightly to check its contents. Inside were small cakes wrapped in paper. He looked at his watch and said that the children's afternoon break would begin soon. Emi asked whether he worked at a school. He shook his head and showed her a card made by children at the town hospital. It thanked him for visiting and sharing stories. The next Friday, Emi brought a book of short stories she had finished and asked whether he thought the children might enjoy hearing one of them.

paragraphs.english: The town's small music room could be booked for one hour at a time. Keiko used it on Wednesday evenings to practice her violin. Every week, she saw a faint pencil mark beside the final hour on the booking sheet. Nobody's name was written there. One evening, her practice ended late, and she stayed to put away chairs. An older man arrived with a toolbox. He checked the loose handle on the door and tightened the screws under a piano bench. When Keiko asked whether he wanted to play music, he laughed and said he preferred listening. He looked at the clock and explained that he waited until the last player had finished. Before leaving, he erased the pencil mark and added one beside the same hour the following week. Keiko thanked him. The next Wednesday, she finished a few minutes early and left a note describing a chair that shook when someone sat on it, so he would not have to check every chair.

paragraphs.english: Rui had practiced his speech many times in his bedroom. He could say every sentence without looking at his notes. On the morning of the school speech meeting, he arrived early and chose a place near the window. As other students entered, he stopped talking and folded his note paper into a small square. His friend Sara asked him a simple question about lunch, but he did not seem to hear it. He kept looking toward the stage and rubbing his hands together. Sara sat beside him and asked whether he wanted to practice the first two lines quietly. They said them together once. Then she asked him to look at her, rather than at all the empty chairs, when he began. During his speech, Rui looked toward the window several times and spoke more steadily after each glance. He remembered all his lines. Afterward, he unfolded the tiny paper and laughed when Sara asked if he still needed to read it.

paragraphs.english: A town moved one bus stop from a hilltop to the bottom of the hill during road repairs. At a public meeting, several residents asked to keep the temporary stop after the work ended. A bus company worker brought a map showing that the original stop was closer to more houses. He expected everyone to agree with moving it back. Then Mrs. Bell described how she walked to the stop with a shopping trolley. The distance from her house was short, but the steep final part took most of her energy. Another resident said the temporary stop had a bench where he could rest. The worker folded his map and began writing notes. At the next meeting, he brought information about slopes, benches, and safe crossing places as well as distances. The company had not made a final decision, but residents said the discussion now included their daily experience. The worker asked them to try two possible routes with him before the next report.

paragraphs.english: At the end of the school term, the gardening club found an envelope in its mailbox. Inside was a small donation and a note saying, Please buy flowers that bloom in autumn. No name was written on it. The club had recently planted spring flowers beside the entrance, and students enjoyed them each morning. However, the school held its open day in October, when those flowers were no longer bright. A week earlier, a former student had visited and asked the club adviser whether the entrance looked colorful in October. The adviser remembered that the visitor now lived far away and usually returned only for open day. The club could not be sure who had sent the envelope. Still, members decided to follow the request and ask a local gardener about suitable plants. They placed a sign near the new bed thanking an unknown supporter. In October, the adviser noticed the former student reading the sign with a quiet smile before entering the school.

paragraphs.english: On a trip with his uncle, Leo had two tickets for an afternoon boat ride. The weather was clear when they bought them in the morning. After lunch, they saw a dark line of clouds above the harbor. At the ticket office, a worker was moving a sign from Afternoon trips to Tomorrow morning. Several passengers were reading notices on their phones. Leo's uncle asked the worker one question, then put the tickets back in his wallet. He suggested visiting the indoor history museum for the rest of the afternoon. Leo did not complain. He had noticed that the flags by the water were now moving strongly and that the smaller boats were tied more tightly to the dock. They spent two hours in the museum learning about old sailing ships. Before leaving, Leo's uncle checked the harbor notice again and wrote a new departure time in his travel notebook. The next morning, they returned early with the same tickets and joined a short line.
paragraphs.translation: 叔父と旅するレオは晴れた朝に午後の船の券二枚を買った。昼食後、黒い雲が出て窓口の係が表示を午後便から翌朝へ変え、客は電話の通知を読んでいた。叔父は一問尋ね券を財布へ戻し屋内の歴史博物館を提案した。旗が強くなびき小船がしっかり係留されたのを見たレオは不満を言わなかった。帆船の歴史を二時間学び、叔父は港の通知を再確認して新しい出発を手帳に記した。翌朝同じ券で早く来て列に並んだ。

title: 箱に残された予備の糸

paragraphs.english: A craft teacher gave each pair of students materials to make a cloth bag. Every box contained cloth, needles, and two colors of thread. There was also an extra length of plain white thread. Most students used only the colorful thread that matched their designs. Mia and Jack finished their bag early and began helping another pair. Suddenly, one handle came loose because its stitches were too far apart. The colorful thread had nearly run out. Jack opened their own box, took out the white thread, and started repairing the handle. He placed the new stitches inside the bag, where they could hardly be seen. At the end of the lesson, the teacher asked what the class had learned besides sewing. Mia held up the empty space where the spare thread had been. Several students nodded and began checking which materials they still had. The teacher asked them to return useful leftovers to a shared cupboard instead of throwing everything away after each project.
paragraphs.translation: 工作の先生は布、針、二色の糸と予備の白糸を各ペアに渡した。多くは色糸だけ使った。早く完成したミアとジャックが別の組を手伝うと、縫い目が粗く持ち手が外れ、色糸も尽きかけた。ジャックは自分たちの白糸を出し見えにくい内側から修理した。終わりに裁縫以外の学びを聞かれ、ミアは予備糸があった空所を示した。他の生徒もうなずき残りを点検した。先生は毎回全部捨てず、使える余りを共有戸棚へ戻すよう求めた。
